messages.subject: Estimates of Occupancy and Abundance for each site
parts:
In unmarked using "occu", "occuRN", and "PCount", how can I get an estimate of occupancy and abundance for each site?

Thanks

-Brian

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: RE: [unmarked] Estimates of Occupancy and Abundance for each site
parts:
My dear Brian,

to be honest, your post deserves the classic "RTFM" answer ! For instance, if you go to the example at the bottom of the help text of occuRN, you find this:
  ## Not run:
    
    
     data(birds)
     woodthrushUMF <- unmarkedFrameOccu(woodthrush.bin)
     # survey occasion-specific detection probabilities
     (fm.wood.rn <- occuRN(~ obsNum ~ 1, woodthrushUMF))
    
     # Empirical Bayes estimates of abundance at each site
     re <- ranef(fm.wood.rn)
     plot(re)
     ## End(Not run)

The more polite answer hence is: use ranef(). But only for occuRN and pcount, since only they model abundance, while occu() models presence/absence and therefore, ranef() gives you the estimate of the presence/absence state at each site. I get the impression that the following article is a obligate read:

Dorazio, R.M. 2007. On the choice of statistical models for estimating occurrence and extinction from animal surveys. Ecology 88: 2773--2782.

If you want the expected occurrence or abundance state (i.e., psi in the occupancy model and lambda in the two abundance models), you can use predict().

Kind regards  --  Marc
